note: Infrastructure-from-Code / workload-spec / platform-capability-API / serverless-runtime LANDSCAPE — the DISTINCT category answering 'are there tools that do purpose/capability/contract-defined programming that completely abstracts cloud-function and K8s-worker programming?'. These tools abstract DEPLOYMENT / WORKLOADS / PLATFORM RESOURCES; none abstracts the capability LIFECYCLE (purpose -> contract -> runtime-selection -> implementation-candidate -> scorecard -> eval-gated promotion -> rollback -> human-boundary-approval). They are CapabilityTask BINDING TARGETS / execution adapters behind a CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; Teleon is the capability-lifecycle CONTROL PLANE ABOVE them, and the local reference binding (teleon.local_function / teleon.local_worker_pool / teleon.capabilitytask_spec / teleon.local_capability_api) stays the stable first path. Discovery != trust; candidate != active; spec/compile target != truth. No raw keys. NEVER active.
verdict: NONE of these does the full Teleon thesis. Infrastructure-from-code (Nitric/Wing/Encore/Klotho) infers cloud resources from application code; workload/app/platform specs (Score/OAM+KubeVela/Radius/Kratix/Crossplane) declare a desired workload/resource shape and a platform fulfils it; serverless/scaler runtimes (Knative/KEDA/Serverless Framework) run and autoscale functions/containers. All abstract WHERE and HOW a workload deploys, not WHETHER a candidate implementation of a stable, purpose-defined capability is promoted on EVIDENCE with a reversible rollback and a human boundary approval. Kratix Promises and Crossplane XRDs get closest to 'capability as a self-service API contract' but stop at provisioning a resource — there is no candidate-vs-baseline scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no truth boundary.
positioning_law: Teleon is the capability-lifecycle CONTROL PLANE ABOVE these infrastructure-from-code / workload-spec / platform-capability-API / serverless-runtime tools. They are CapabilityTask binding targets and execution adapters behind a CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; the CapabilityTask/PurposeTask contract, runtime selection, side-by-side candidates, evidence/scorecards, eval-gated promotion, reversible rollback, and human boundary approval all live ABOVE the binding target. Teleon is NOT another infrastructure-from-code framework, NOT another workload spec, NOT another platform-engineering orchestrator, NOT a serverless runtime: it binds CapabilityTasks DOWN onto these targets while the capability lifecycle stays in Teleon. The local reference binding stays the stable first path; every target here is one switchable peer with a governed local-equivalent fallback, never a second control plane.
teleon_local_equivalents: teleon.local_function@v1 — the local reference function binding (stable first path; a CapabilityTask runs in-process before any cloud function target)
teleon.local_worker_pool@v1 — the local reference worker/queue binding (stable first path before any K8s/serverless scaler)
teleon.capabilitytask_spec@v1 — the CapabilityTask/PurposeTask contract that is EXPORTED to a workload spec (Score/OAM), never replaced by it
teleon.local_capability_api@v1 — the local capability-as-self-service-API surface that a Kratix Promise / Crossplane XRD / Radius resource type would bind to, not own

cross_reference.note: Durable-workflow + agent-runtime backends are cataloged SEPARATELY and are NOT re-added here. Temporal/DBOS/Hatchet/Inngest/Trigger.dev/Dapr/ARK/kagent/AgentScope/agent-sandbox live in teleon_runtime_landscape.json; Restate/Prefect/Kestra/Windmill/Flyte/Ray/Modal/Cloudflare/Letta/LangGraph/Bedrock/Vertex live in teleon_adjacent_extended.json. A CapabilityTask can ALSO bind to those (Temporal-workflow / Modal-function) — see the binding map in _repos/teleon/context/research/capability-binding-and-ifc-landscape.md.
cross_reference.teleon_runtime_landscape: architecture/teleon_runtime_landscape.json (durable-workflow + K8s/agent runtimes: Temporal, DBOS, Dapr, Hatchet, Inngest, Trigger.dev, ARK, kagent, AgentScope, agent-sandbox)
cross_reference.teleon_adjacent_extended: architecture/teleon_adjacent_extended.json (Restate, Prefect, Kestra, Windmill, Flyte, Ray, Modal, Cloudflare Workflows/Agents, Letta, LangGraph, Bedrock AgentCore, Vertex Agent Engine)

entries.name: Kratix
entries.license_note: Open-source core Apache 2.0 (Syntasso). Syntasso Kratix Enterprise (SKE) is a separate commercial product (portal/IaC integrations, enterprise Promise marketplace, support).
entries.what_it_abstracts: Platform engineers package a platform capability (database, CI/CD pipeline, K8s cluster, VM, third-party service) as a Promise — a self-service, governed Kubernetes API. A Promise declares its dependencies, an API for how a consumer requests it, the workflows that provision it, and destination rules for where resources land. This is the single closest match to 'capability as a self-service API contract'.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: A Promise PROVISIONS a resource when requested; it does not declare a purpose-defined capability whose IMPLEMENTATION evolves while the contract stays stable. No side-by-side candidate implementations, no scorecard, no EVIDENCE-gated promotion, no reversible rollback object, no human boundary-expansion approval, no Baltor-style truth boundary. It answers 'give me a database', not 'is this candidate way of fulfilling the capability good enough to promote?'.
entries.differentiation_move: A Teleon CapabilityTask binds DOWN onto a Kratix Promise as one platform-capability-API target; Teleon keeps the stable contract + candidate comparison + eval-gated promotion + rollback ABOVE the Promise. Do not let Promises become a second capability registry.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Closest to the capability-contract idea but still resource-provisioning, not capability-lifecycle. Candidate platform-capability-API binding target behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; never the Teleon control plane, never a second capability registry. The local capability-API surface stays the stable first path.

entries.name: Radius (radapp.io)
entries.license_note: CNCF Sandbox (accepted 2024-04-16); Apache 2.0, IP owned by CNCF. Microsoft-originated.
entries.what_it_abstracts: A cloud-native, cloud-agnostic application platform: developers describe an application and its dependencies; platform engineers define organization-specific Resource Types and implement them with Recipes (Terraform configs or Bicep templates) per Environment, so the same app definition maps to dev vs prod infrastructure. Strong 'platform-defined resource type' contract.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Resource Types + Recipes select WHICH infrastructure fulfils a declared resource; there is no candidate-implementation comparison of a capability against a baseline, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no human boundary approval, no truth boundary. It abstracts the resource graph, not the capability lifecycle.
entries.differentiation_move: A CapabilityTask binds to a Radius Resource Type via its Recipe as a resource-composition target; the Recipe says HOW to provision, Teleon's evidence + promotion decide WHETHER the candidate capability ships. Radius's Resource-Type-with-Recipes split is external CONFIRMATION that a stable contract above swappable implementations is the right shape.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate resource-composition / platform-capability-API binding target behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; Recipes are HOW-to-provision detail, not the capability lifecycle. Never a second control plane; local capability-API surface stays the stable first path.

entries.name: Crossplane
entries.what_it_abstracts: Build custom control planes on Kubernetes: a CompositeResourceDefinition (XRD) defines the schema of a new platform API, a Composition translates that API into a graph of Managed Resources, and consumers create a claim to request it. Lets a platform team publish their own infrastructure APIs the way cloud vendors do.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: XRD + Composition + claim provision and reconcile cloud/infra resources toward a desired state; there is no purpose/capability whose implementation is selected from candidates on EVIDENCE, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback-as-object, no human boundary approval, no truth boundary. It is a control plane for RESOURCES, not for capability LIFECYCLE.
entries.differentiation_move: A CapabilityTask can bind to a Crossplane XRD/claim as a resource-composition target; Crossplane's 'publish your own API' validates the contract-above-implementation shape, but Teleon adds candidate comparison + eval-gated promotion + rollback + truth boundary that a reconcile-to-desired-state control plane does not have.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate resource-composition / platform-capability-API binding target; 'custom control plane' here means a RESOURCE control plane, NOT the capability-lifecycle control plane. Never adopt Crossplane as the Teleon control plane or a second capability registry.

entries.name: Score (score.dev)
entries.license_note: CNCF Sandbox; Apache 2.0. Reference implementations score-compose (Docker Compose) and score-k8s (Kubernetes manifests); score-helm and Cloud Run / Fly.io are additional targets.
entries.what_it_abstracts: A platform-agnostic, container-based WORKLOAD specification: define a workload once in one YAML file, then a Score Implementation CLI translates it to Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, Google Cloud Run, Fly.io, etc. Eliminates per-platform config drift between environments.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Score describes a single workload's resources/ports/dependencies for translation to a target; it has no notion of a purpose, no candidate implementations, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. It is a portable DEPLOYMENT description, not a capability lifecycle.
entries.differentiation_move: Teleon EXPORTS a CapabilityTask's selected implementation to a Score workload spec for portable deployment; the CapabilityTask contract is exported TO Score, never replaced BY it. Score's 'define once, translate to many targets' is direct validation of runtime-neutral binding.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate workload-spec export target behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; a Score file is a deployment description Teleon EMITS, not the stable capability contract. teleon.capabilitytask_spec@v1 stays the source of truth.

entries.name: Nitric
entries.license_note: Open-source core Apache 2.0; multi-language (TS/Python/Go/etc.). Pre-built providers deploy via Pulumi or Terraform. Paid offerings around support / hosted control plane being developed.
entries.what_it_abstracts: Infrastructure-from-code: you write application code declaring resource requirements (APIs, queues, topics, key/value, storage, schedules) and Nitric INFERS and provisions the cloud infrastructure, deploying the same code to AWS (Lambda/API Gateway/SQS/SNS/DynamoDB), GCP, Azure, or your own Kubernetes cluster — no hand-written Terraform.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Nitric abstracts cloud-function/queue/storage PROVISIONING from code; it has no purpose/capability contract decoupled from implementation, no candidate comparison, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. It abstracts WHERE the code deploys, not WHETHER a candidate capability is promoted.
entries.differentiation_move: A CapabilityTask whose runtime selection lands on a cloud function can COMPILE its implementation to Nitric (which then targets AWS/GCP/Azure/K8s); Nitric is the cloud-portable compile target, Teleon owns the contract + evidence + promotion. The local function binding stays the stable first path.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate infrastructure-from-code compile target behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; abstracts deployment, not capability lifecycle. teleon.local_function@v1 stays the stable first path; Nitric is one switchable cloud target.

entries.name: Encore (encore.dev)
entries.license_note: Open-source framework/parser/compiler/runtime/CLI under Mozilla Public License 2.0 (self-hostable). Encore Cloud is a separate commercial managed deployment platform. Supports TypeScript and Go; deploys into your own AWS or GCP account.
entries.what_it_abstracts: Backend infrastructure-from-code: declare infrastructure (services, databases, Pub/Sub, cron) directly in application code; Encore parses it and provisions everything per environment in your own AWS/GCP account with no Terraform/Pulumi. Runs the whole backend locally with real services/DBs/Pub/Sub via one command.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Encore abstracts backend service + infra PROVISIONING from code; no purpose/capability contract above evolving implementations, no candidate comparison, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. It is a backend framework, not a capability-lifecycle control plane.
entries.differentiation_move: A CapabilityTask can compile a backend-service implementation to Encore as one infra-from-code target (AWS/GCP); Encore's strong local-dev story aligns with our local-first stance, but Teleon's contract + evidence + promotion sit above Encore's provisioning.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate backend-infra-from-code compile target behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; abstracts backend deployment, not capability lifecycle. Local function/worker binding stays the stable first path.

entries.name: Wing (Winglang)
entries.license_note: MIT. Still PRE-RELEASE / early development as of 2026: AWS fully supported (Terraform engine), GCP/Azure partial; ships a local cloud simulator, test framework, IDE extension. Wing Cloud is the company behind it.
entries.what_it_abstracts: A cloud-oriented programming language unifying infrastructure (preflight) and runtime (inflight) code in one language; compiles to Terraform/CloudFormation and runs locally in a full cloud SIMULATOR (functions, queues, buckets, etc.). Abstracts the function/queue/bucket primitives behind language constructs.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Wing abstracts the cloud RESOURCE/runtime split into a language; it has no purpose/capability contract, no candidate comparison, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. A language for cloud apps, not a capability lifecycle. Pre-release maturity is an adoption caution.
entries.differentiation_move: Wing's local cloud SIMULATOR is the most interesting signal — it validates a local-equivalent path for cloud primitives, exactly the teleon.local_function pattern. Treat Wing as a research compile-target/simulator reference; Teleon's contract + promotion stay above the language.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Research-stage cloud-oriented-language compile target; pre-release, AWS-leaning. Study the local simulator as a local-equivalent reference; never the Teleon control plane. teleon.local_function@v1 stays the stable first path.

entries.name: Klotho (Klotho Engine)
entries.license_note: Repo widely reported as Apache 2.0 but project is ARCHIVED — license treated as unverified pending re-check of the archived repo. Vendor (Klotho/klo.dev) pivoted to InfraCopilot (a conversational IaC editor built on the same Klotho Engine).
entries.what_it_abstracts: Infrastructure-from-code that took annotated application code and generated cloud infrastructure (IaC) by reasoning about the architecture via the open-source Klotho Engine; aimed to let developers write code and have cloud resources inferred.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Same category gap as the other IfC tools (no purpose/capability contract, no candidate comparison, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary) AND the project is no longer actively developed, so it cannot be a live binding target.
entries.differentiation_move: Keep Klotho as an ARCHIVED reference for the infrastructure-from-code idea (code-to-IaC inference); do NOT bind to it as a live target. Its existence-then-archival is evidence the IfC category churns and that owning the capability lifecycle (not the codegen) is the durable position.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: ARCHIVED / no longer actively developed — reference only, never a live binding target. Re-verify license against the archived repo before quoting it. teleon.local_function@v1 stays the stable first path.

entries.name: OAM + KubeVela
entries.license_note: OAM spec + KubeVela both CNCF, Apache 2.0; KubeVela CNCF Incubating (since 2023-02-27), originated at Alibaba. KubeVela's delivery workflow is powered by the Open Application Model.
entries.what_it_abstracts: The Open Application Model is a higher-level, application-centric abstraction (components + traits + policies + workflow) for modeling cloud-native apps across hybrid/multi-cloud; KubeVela implements OAM as a modern application delivery platform that hides Kubernetes details behind a simple app definition and delivery workflow.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: OAM/KubeVela model and DELIVER an application across environments; there is no purpose-defined capability whose implementation is selected from candidates on EVIDENCE, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback-as-object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. It is an app-delivery model, not a capability lifecycle.
entries.differentiation_move: Teleon can EXPORT a CapabilityTask's chosen implementation to an OAM application/KubeVela definition as an app-delivery target; OAM's components/traits separation validates app-centric abstraction, but Teleon's eval-gated promotion + rollback live above the delivery workflow.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate app-delivery-model export target behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; an OAM app definition is a delivery description Teleon emits, not the capability contract. teleon.capabilitytask_spec@v1 stays the source of truth.

entries.name: Knative
entries.license_note: CNCF Graduated 2025-09-11; Apache 2.0. Knative Serving (request-driven autoscaling incl. scale-to-zero, revisions, routing) + Eventing.
entries.what_it_abstracts: A Kubernetes-native serverless runtime: deploy and run serverless/event-driven workloads on K8s with request-driven autoscaling (including scale-to-zero), revisions, and traffic routing — abstracts the autoscaling/routing/networking plumbing of running a function-as-a-service on Kubernetes.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: Knative RUNS and autoscales a serverless service; it has no capability contract, no candidate comparison, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion (its revisions/traffic split are deployment routing, not evidence-gated capability promotion), no rollback-as-capability-object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary.
entries.differentiation_move: A CapabilityTask whose runtime selection picks K8s-serverless binds to a Knative Service as an execution adapter; Knative handles scale-to-zero/routing, Teleon decides which candidate runs and whether it is promoted. The local function binding stays the stable first path.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate K8s-serverless execution adapter behind CapabilityTaskBindingProvider; Knative revisions/traffic-split are deployment routing, NOT Teleon's eval-gated promotion. teleon.local_function@v1 stays the stable first path.

entries.name: KEDA
entries.license_note: CNCF Graduated (2023); Apache 2.0. 70+ built-in scalers; scales any container in Kubernetes to/from zero based on event sources; acts as a K8s metrics server.
entries.what_it_abstracts: Kubernetes event-driven autoscaling: scale any container to and from zero based on event source metrics (queues, streams, databases, telemetry, etc.) via a ScaledObject CRD — abstracts the scaling decision for an event-driven worker so it costs nothing when idle.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: KEDA only decides HOW MANY replicas of a worker run given an event load; it has no capability contract, no candidate implementation, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. It is a scaler, the narrowest slice here.
entries.differentiation_move: A CapabilityTask bound to a K8s worker can attach KEDA as the scaler (scale-to-zero on an event source); KEDA is purely the autoscaling adapter under a worker binding, Teleon owns everything above it. The local worker pool stays the stable first path.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Candidate event-driven SCALER behind a worker binding; narrowest slice — autoscaling only, never a capability plane. teleon.local_worker_pool@v1 stays the stable first path.

entries.name: Serverless Framework
entries.license_note: LICENSE FLAG: Serverless Framework CLI v4+ is under a proprietary license requiring login / a license key (free for orgs under $2M annual revenue; paid above). v3 and earlier remain MIT. Treat as a reference, not a wrap-by-default target, due to the v4 license + auth requirement.
entries.what_it_abstracts: A YAML-config framework that packages and deploys serverless functions and managed-service resources (primarily AWS Lambda, plus other clouds) — abstracts the packaging/deploy/IAM/event-wiring of functions-as-a-service behind a serverless.yml.
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: It deploys functions + resources from a config; no capability contract, no candidate comparison, no scorecard, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback-as-object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary. Plus the v4 license/auth requirement makes it a constrained target.
entries.differentiation_move: Listed as the incumbent serverless-deploy REFERENCE that defines the 'deploy functions from a spec' surface Teleon binds above; prefer Apache/MIT targets (Score/Nitric) for actual binding given the v4 license. Teleon's contract + promotion stay runtime-neutral.
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: Reference incumbent only — v4+ proprietary + license-key/auth requirement makes it a constrained binding target; prefer Apache/MIT compile targets. Never the Teleon control plane; teleon.local_function@v1 stays the stable first path.
